clue.text: Artist in charge in route through ring

indicators.note: the second 'in' places one piece inside the other, as a thing sits within its holder

parts.note: a pass is a route through mountains
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A painter somebody has put in charge of a road that runs through a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two 'in's: the first belongs to the phrase in charge, the second tells you to insert IC into PASS, with O added last.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter behind Cubism, a famous example of an artist.

clue.text: Penny inclined to be easily influenced

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
liable to do something means inclined to do it

explanation.surface: Someone called Penny is the sort who gets talked round by anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a woman's name, but here it is the coin's abbreviation P, placed before LIABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliable bends easily, and a pliable person is readily swayed by others' opinions.

clue.text: Quietens many with charitable gifts

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
alms are money or food given to the poor

explanation.surface: Handing out donations to lots of people keeps them quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Many as C (a hundred in Roman numerals) is a crossword convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm someone is to soothe or settle them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Steal fruit then you start to make cider

parts.note: to scrump is British slang for stealing apples from an orchard

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe for cider that starts with pinching apples from someone's orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrumping is a British word for stealing apples from trees, which neatly fits a cider surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is a rough, strong farmhouse cider from the West Country of England.

clue.text: Readily available where palm is?

definitions.meaning: the everyday phrase for something close by and ready to use
read literally: the palm is part of the hand, so it sits there

explanation.walkthrough: Palm suggests a tree, but here it is the inside of the hand; the question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Help that is close by and ready to use is idiomatically said to be at hand, nearby.

clue.text: Commercial to choose to take on

parts.note: an ad is a commercial on TV or radio
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: A company deciding which advertisement to run.
explanation.walkthrough: Commercial looks like an adjective describing a business, but it is the noun: an advert, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Adopting a plan, a child or a policy means accepting it as your own responsibility.

clue.text: Ezra struggling, going round the bend, was blue

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece wraps another
something struggling is thrashing about, so its letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
a U-bend is a pipe bend, so U can stand for bend

explanation.surface: A man named Ezra having a hard time, going mad and feeling depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Going round the bend and blue both suggest a state of mind, but the bend is a U, and blue is the colour, not sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is the bright clear shade of a cloudless sky, one particular hue of the colour.

clue.text: Very English Tosca performance with sets of eight notes

indicators.note: a performance is a production, so the letters are worked into a new staging

parts.note: v is the abbreviation for very
E is the abbreviation for English
Puccini's opera, used here as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An especially English staging of Puccini's opera, full of musical scales.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface is apt: Tosca is an opera, yet its letters plus V and E simply rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave spans a scale from one note to the next of the same name, counting both ends.

clue.text: Royal house in situ, dormant

indicators.note: the answer is in the following words, lying inside their letters

parts.note: runs across the comma between the two words

explanation.surface: A royal residence still standing where it always was, but asleep and unused.
explanation.walkthrough: In situ is a Latin phrase meaning in its original place, which makes the 'in' look part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal dynasty of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I, 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Loafer left in dire trouble

indicators.note: placing something in another puts it within, so one piece is held by another
things in trouble are in disarray, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A layabout abandoned when things are desperate.
explanation.walkthrough: Loafer could be a shoe, but here it means a lazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is someone who lazes about avoiding work, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Searched around a house perhaps, that's full of ghosts

definitions.text: house perhaps, that's full of ghosts

indicators.note: to be around something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to hunt is to search
taken as it stands

explanation.surface: Exploring a spooky old house that is full of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on from the wordplay and leans on the stock phrase 'haunted house'; the 'perhaps' admits a house is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A place visited by spirits or ghosts is said to be haunted, as in the familiar phrase.

clue.text: Someone required in union to get batsmen out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, as in a put-out joint, signalling rearrangement

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A team needs a player who can dismiss the opposing batters in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface makes 'out' look like a dismissal and 'union' look like a trade or sporting union; the union is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding the groom's chief attendant, who holds the rings and gives a speech, is essential.

clue.text: Immature swimmer always circling lake

indicators.note: circling means going all the way around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A young swimmer who keeps doing laps round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Swimmer suggests a person, but it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a fish in its juvenile stage migrating up rivers.

clue.text: It could be the beginning or be my undoing

indicators.note: undoing something takes it apart, so the letters are loosened and remade

parts.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

explanation.surface: A dramatic line: this moment may launch me or ruin me.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is three little words, easy to skip over as filler in a melodramatic sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is the earliest stage of an organism's development, the start of a new life.

clue.text: Points to wartime ordeal for reindeer

indicators.note: one thing added to another is attached after it, fixing the order

parts.note: the Blitz was the German bombing of Britain in 1940-41
E and N are two compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: Someone pointing to a wartime hardship as fitting for a reindeer.
explanation.walkthrough: Points as compass directions is a standard convention; 'to' puts them after the second piece, not before.
explanation.definitionFit: Blitzen is one of Santa Claus's eight flying reindeer in the Christmas poem and song.

clue.text: Short sleep in cosiest armchair

indicators.note: the answer lies in the next words, contained inside their letters

parts.note: spans the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Taking a nap in the comfiest chair in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in the scene: a nap in the armchair, lying across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is a brief afternoon nap, a custom in Spain and other hot countries.

clue.text: Form of an atom that's kept stoop crooked

indicators.note: to have kept something is to hold it inside, so one piece contains another

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters

explanation.surface: A physics definition oddly followed by someone keeping a bent posture.
explanation.walkthrough: That's as IE (that is) is a convention worth knowing; the two letters split to hold the rearranged five.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopes are variants of one chemical element that differ in their number of neutrons.

clue.text: Melissa straying, without direction

indicators.note: straying means wandering off course, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A woman called Melissa wandering about with no idea where she is heading.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface acts out the meaning: Melissa straying is wandering with no goal, and her name holds its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless means lacking purpose or goal, drifting with no particular course or plan.

clue.text: A school jacket nearly on fire

indicators.note: almost all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a blazer is a jacket, often part of a British school uniform

explanation.surface: A pupil's uniform jacket has very nearly caught fire.
explanation.walkthrough: A blazer is the smart jacket worn as British school uniform; 'nearly' trims its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaze means burning fiercely, the same as being on fire.

clue.text: Raise one in the army

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is held by another

parts.note: a host is an army, an old sense as in heavenly host
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Promoting a single soldier in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: Host for army is an old sense worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to lift up, often with ropes or tackle, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Dress custom

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a tailor-made garment; split them into two separate nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a religious garment worn by nuns and a settled practice done routinely.

clue.text: Reportedly shown up incorporating overused plot device

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, backwards
to incorporate is to contain within, so the answer is held inside a word

parts.note: letters two to six of the word, read backwards

explanation.surface: Allegedly a writer was exposed for relying on a clichéd plot twist.
explanation.walkthrough: Reportedly looks like a homophone indicator but is the source word itself; the answer runs backwards inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a common or cliched theme or motif in stories, recycled by many writers.

clue.text: Awful slobs have order to prosper

indicators.note: awful means terrible, so the letters are in a terrible state and need fixing

parts.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters
the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Lazy slobs told they must get on and make something of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Order as OM (Order of Merit, a British honour) is a common convention; 'have' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to flourish or develop well, like a plant coming into flower.

clue.text: Dressing evidently protects a superficial burn

indicators.note: to protect something is to shelter it inside, so the answer is enclosed

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A first-aid note: a dressing clearly covers a minor burn.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes dressing a bandage, which really does protect a burn.
explanation.definitionFit: A singe is a slight scorch to the surface of hair, cloth or skin, not a deep wound.

clue.text: Graduate encircling a menagerie, final check for weapon

indicators.note: encircling means surrounding on all sides, so one piece holds the rest

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
taken as it stands
a zoo is a collection of animals

indicators.note: final means last, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A graduate taking charge of a zoo does a last inspection of the firearms.
explanation.walkthrough: A graduate is nearly always BA or MA in crosswords; here it splits open to hold three smaller pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazooka is a portable shoulder-fired rocket launcher used against tanks.

clue.text: Little weight for cat

definitions.meaning: a small imperial unit of mass
a big cat of the mountains

explanation.walkthrough: The snow leopard sense is a less familiar one, much loved by setters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a sixteenth of a pound, and also the old name for the snow leopard.

clue.text: Metal, for example, turning colour

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: turning round points the other way, so the letters face backwards

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: A piece of metal, say, changing its colour as it tarnishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like it offers Metal as an example, but it is EG, which is then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a faint trace of a hue, and as a verb means to tint slightly.

clue.text: Teams essential to chapel evensong

indicators.note: essential means belonging to the essence or core, so the answer sits inside

parts.note: runs across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Groups of people who are vital to the evening service at a chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket sides field eleven players, so a side is often called by that number.
